tldr: Canadian competitor news is thin today: BMO's quantum/AI claim is the only direct-competitor move, and the rest of the Canadian items are rate and card roundups. The bigger signals are elsewhere: investing access is widening (Kalshi moving into stocks, B3 listing a low-minimum Anthropic BDR, Mercado Pago embedding investing in its app), while outages and data leaks keep reliability and security in focus.
themes: Low-barrier access to investing and hot IPOs
Non-bank players moving into brokerage and banking

highlights.headline: Kalshi is buying New York broker FB Securities to launch stock and ETF trading.
highlights.why: A prediction-market exchange is becoming a full broker, so more non-bank platforms will compete for the same self-directed investors Simplii's trading offer serves.

highlights.headline: B3 listed an Anthropic BDR (ANTH34) to trade alongside the company's Nasdaq IPO, with a minimum investment reported at under R$100.
highlights.why: Local, same-day, small-ticket access to a high-profile US IPO sets an expectation that Canadian self-directed investors may start to share.

highlights.headline: Mercado Pago now lets users invest in pesos in its app via CEDEARs, taking on the broker Cocos.
highlights.why: A payments app is adding investing to its everyday money tools, a pattern to watch for Wealthsimple-style bundling of spending, saving and investing.

highlights.headline: BMO claims a quantum computing breakthrough, saying it could help AI models find the most relevant information in complex datasets.
highlights.why: This is a direct Canadian competitor positioning itself as a tech and AI leader. It is an early claim with no customer-facing product yet, but it is worth tracking.
